_meta.session: MacBook live, race-day continuation after Windows handoff
_meta.scope: All 8 algo-scored races (R6 Arabian skipped). R10-R12 to come.
_meta.purpose: Empirical accounting of algo predictions vs reality + per-signal outcomes. Source of truth for which patterns to trust beyond N=1.

1.lesson: LONE-BEYER TRAP. #4 had a single Beyer of 62 off 108-day layoff. Algo punished ability to ×0.70; market priced him 4.5/1.
1.fix_shipped: lone_beyer_protection in _ability_value defers to Prime Power when ≤1 Beyer figure

2.lesson: SHARP 9.4× BET-DOWN. #2 went 15/1 ML → 1.6 live. Massive market signal.
2.fix_shipped: _sharp_money_signals: high ML/live ratio pulls bias/ability factors toward 1.0
2.trainer_gap: Gregory D. Foley (R2 winner) was missing from TIER_TRAINERS until this session

3.lesson: Pool-disparity flag's first morning hit. Chalk-trap detection working in claiming.

4.flag_outcome: HELD (#8 was 4th in photo, out of top 3)
4.lesson: BORING-BALANCED + TOP CONNECTIONS WINS CHAOS. #12 Breaking Hearts: no extreme signals, top trainer+jockey (Cherie DeVaux + Jose Ortiz). Algo over-weights signal extremes, under-rates competence.

5.lesson: FIRST clean forward exacta. Algo v2 (Tweaks A+B) just shipped. Closer-friendly track-bias override (Tweak B) caught the day's pace pattern.

7.tri_box_lost: Algo recommended 1-4-5 box. Came 1-7-5. #7 Vow to Resiliency was algo's #4 at 10%.
7.lesson: Top-1 reliable on cleaner races. Under-spread still noisy on board horses outside top-3 algo picks.

8.lesson: Second clean forward exacta of the day. Algo's top 2 hit 1-2 in order. R8 winner's trainer (Robert Hess Jr.) is NOT in TIER_TRAINERS — top connections aren't strictly necessary when other signals align (Beyer 94, Prime Power 123.9, Irad Ortiz Jr.).

9.top3_hit: partial (2/3 — #8 #4 in algo top-3, #5 was algo #5)
9.lesson: Chalk-doubt's first miss. Hypothesis: doesn't generalize to stakes-grade chalks with top connections (Asmussen/J.Ortiz). BUT secondary board signals (P>W and show-spike) both nailed the 2nd and 3rd. The flag's structure may need to split: (a) chalk-doesn't-win — segment to claiming/maiden/allowance; (b) smart-money-board — applies broadly. (a) is 4-1; (b) is 2-0.

totals_through_R9.post_v2_top1_rate: 4/4 (R5 + R7 + R8 + R9 since algo v2 shipped)
totals_through_R9.ml_chalk_baseline_top1: 6/8 — 75% (chalk has been winning frequently today; not a chalk-trap day overall)
totals_through_R9.wait: Through R5 chalk was 1/5 = 20% (chalk-trap day pattern); R7-R9 chalk was 3/3 (chalk recovered). The track 'pivoted' mid-card.

validated_strong.name: smart_money_board
validated_strong.claim: When place-pool % > win-pool % by 3+pts on a non-chalk horse, that horse hits the board
validated_strong.evidence: 2/2 today (R5 #12, R9 #5). Both correctly predicted as 2nd-place finishers.
validated_strong.actionable: Add a top-3-finish probability boost (separate from win prob) for these horses. Use in trifecta/super construction.
validated_strong.n_for_validation: Need 50+ races per handoff doc, but 2/2 is encouraging — validation track.

validated_strong.name: show_pool_spike
validated_strong.claim: When show-pool size grows >3× in <10 min approaching post on one horse, that horse hits the board
validated_strong.actionable: Polling /pools every 5 min in the 30 min before post + tracking deltas would give us this signal automatically.
validated_strong.n_for_validation: N=1. Track but don't code yet.

validated_strong.name: boring_balanced_chaos_winner
validated_strong.claim: In wide-open chaos races, the horse with top-tier trainer+jockey but NO extreme signals (Beyer / PP / class) often wins
validated_strong.evidence: R4 #12 Breaking Hearts (DeVaux + Jose Ortiz, no signal extremes, won at 5/1 in chaos race).
validated_strong.actionable: Detect chaos race (top-1 score < 25% or field >10), then scan for horses with top-tier trainer+jockey AND no Beyer/PP/style extremes. Boost their score modestly (~5%).

validated_moderate.name: algo_post_v2_top1
validated_moderate.claim: Since algo v2 shipped (Tweaks A+B), top-1 hits at 4/4 = 100%
validated_moderate.caveat: Small sample. Includes R8/R9 which were also chalk-leaning races where algo+market agreed.
validated_moderate.actionable: Continue using v2. Backtest on 4-25 + 4-26 cards once results.json includes them.

validated_moderate.name: algo_top3_under_spread
validated_moderate.claim: Algo top-3 catches the eventual board 87.5% of the time. The 2nd-3rd algo picks are reliable for board.
validated_moderate.evidence: 7/8 today. Exception: R7 (#7 Vow at algo's 4th hit 2nd, breaking 1-4-5 tri box).
validated_moderate.actionable: All exotic structures should ALWAYS include algo top-4 (not just top-3). 1-extra-horse super box catches the R7-style boundary cases.

needs_segmentation.name: chalk_doubt
needs_segmentation.claim_v1: Top-3 odds horse with W-P > 5pts won't win
needs_segmentation.evidence_so_far_after_R10: 4 hits (R1-R4, all claiming/maiden/turf maiden) / 2 misses (R9 stakes Asmussen/J.Ortiz, R10 stakes D'Amato/Prat). Both stakes failures back-to-back.
needs_segmentation.proposed_v2: Apply chalk-doubt only when race purse < $100K (excludes stakes) AND chalk's trainer is NOT in top-tier list. Test on next 30 cards.
needs_segmentation.real_time_lesson_R10: I (Mac Claude) over-rode the algo's default super box recommendation (2-9-6-1) by substituting #8 for #9. The algo had #9 in its top-3 — the flag's fade override was wrong twice in a row in stakes context. CONCLUSION: trust the algo's full top-N over a single-signal override when the segmentation hasn't been validated.
needs_segmentation.n_for_validation: 6 fires total (4 hits + 2 misses). Need 30+ to test segmentation; current sample is suggestive but not conclusive.

proposed_changes_data_backed.change: Always include algo top-4 (not top-3) in trifecta/super box construction in _build_recommendations
proposed_changes_data_backed.rationale: Top-3 hit rate is 87.5%, but the 12.5% miss (R7 #7 Vow) was algo's #4. Adding the 4th horse covers that boundary case at marginal extra cost ($0.50 → $1.00 on a 4-horse super box vs 3-horse).
proposed_changes_data_backed.risk: Slightly higher per-race outlay. Cuts effective EV per box but boosts hit rate.

proposed_changes_data_backed.change: Add `_board_signal_factor` for smart-money-board and show-pool spike — separate from win-prob
proposed_changes_data_backed.rationale: These signals predict BOARD finishes, not WIN. The current scoring model is win-prob only. To use these signals correctly, we need a top-3 secondary score for exotic construction.
proposed_changes_data_backed.risk: Requires expanding the scoring schema. Don't ship mid-card. Plan for post-card.

proposed_changes_data_backed.change: Auto-poll /pools every 5 min in the 30 min before each race; capture deltas
proposed_changes_data_backed.rationale: Show-pool spike was identified manually today. Automation is needed to catch it real-time.
proposed_changes_data_backed.risk: Engineering work. Cortex notes flagged this as the highest-leverage signal we don't have automated.

proposed_changes_data_backed.change: Add `Robert B. Hess Jr.` and any other R8/R9/R10/R11/R12 winning trainers to TIER_TRAINERS post-card
proposed_changes_data_backed.rationale: R8 winning trainer Hess wasn't on the list. Pattern: every CD opening week, there are ~3 trainers who pop that aren't in our list. Adding them post-card is the right cadence.
proposed_changes_data_backed.risk: None. Validate by win frequency at meet.

do_not_change_mid_card: Stable algo state lets us collect clean live signal. Document, don't ship, until R12 done.

_meta_lesson_R10_post.trigger: After R10 #9 Maximum Bourbon won (algo's #2, market chalk), realizing I'd advised fading both R9 #8 and R10 #9 based on the chalk-doubt flag overlay.
_meta_lesson_R10_post.lesson: DO NOT OVERRIDE THE CORE ALGO SCORE WITH A SECONDARY HEURISTIC THAT HASN'T BEEN VALIDATED AT SCALE. The algo's score combines Beyer (z-scored within field), Prime Power, jockey/trainer tier, market price (Benter anchor), and post bias. That's a model trained against many races. The chalk-doubt flag is an N=4 morning overlay. Letting it override the core was overfitting to recent noise.
evidence_against_overlay_override: Algo top-2 in last 5 algo-scored races: 5-for-5 (R5, R7, R8, R9, R10).
Algo top-3 across all 8 algo-scored races today: 7-for-8 = 87.5%.
Both 'flag failures' (R9, R10) had the algo's actual top pick still hit. The math wasn't broken; the overlay was wrong.

framework_correction.old: Chalk-doubt flag fires → fade horse from win, override algo if needed.
framework_correction.new: Chalk-doubt flag fires → SECONDARY signal. Use to DETECT smart-money board candidates (P>W, show-spike) for under-spread construction. Do NOT use to override algo's win-prob ranking on the chalk itself, especially in stakes races with top-tier connections.
framework_correction.rule: Flag overlay can REORDER top-3 by ±10% confidence, but cannot drop a horse out of the algo's top-3 unless the algo itself ranks them low to begin with.

_meta_lesson_R10_post.remaining_races: R11 (Mamzelle G3) + R12 (MC 50000): back algo's top picks straight. No flag-based overrides for the rest of the card.
_meta_lesson_R10_post.code_change_revised: Don't add the stakes-segmentation guard yet. Instead, soften the chalk-doubt penalty in _pool_disparity_factor: cap the penalty at 5-10% reduction (was probably 25%+ effective when paired with the algo's Beyer/PP score). The signal has SOME value (still 4/6 = 67%), but it shouldn't dominate the score.
